historical_reviews.deepseek: Does not capture authoritative threshold/window values, injection cardinality or before/after counters and assumes Linux dmesg on Windows.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly makes the counter timeline primary but does not explicitly flag the source's `(Inaccurate)` BIOS labels as unusable parameters.
historical_reviews.related_cases: A generic memory CE proves injection, not that a bucket decayed without crossing its threshold.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Counts, timers and destructive target tuples are material parameters that cannot be guessed.

original_test_intent: Prove that each approved memory controller's correctable-error leaky bucket increments below threshold and then decays by the specified amount after the configured time window, without service loss or fault-light assertion.
original_method: The FAE supplies authoritative threshold/window semantics, maps the controller target and chooses a bounded CE count with margin below threshold. Pre-count, each injection timestamp, post-injection count and post-window count are captured from the same counter source, then correlated with slot logs, indicators and system health before restoration.
manual_activity: The FAE must set the approved bucket values, choose each controller tuple, run the bounded injection and release sequence and restore BIOS state. The agent may timestamp and validate the counter decay from supplied read-only evidence.
required_inputs: Authoritative threshold, time-window units and counter-decay algorithm/source
ITP/CScripts build/hash and injectMemError CE semantics
Approved injection count/margin/timing and BMC/UEFI/indicator/health oracle
Dedicated-SUT approval, abort, recovery and BIOS restoration plan
safety_requirements: Dedicated idle SUT with stable power and console
Record counter baseline without clearing historical evidence
Use an approved count demonstrably below threshold for one target at a time
Abort before threshold or on counter mismatch, UCE, crash or health change
No retry; restore bucket/EDKII settings and verify no residual error
agent_execution_scope: Verify target/counter captures, time intervals and arithmetic; collect read-only platform evidence
Do not set BIOS values, choose tuples/counts, inject, resume/reset/retry or set verdict
engineer_actions: Define bucket algorithm and authoritative counter
Set count/window/decay acceptance and log expectations

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Keyword logs cannot prove numerical bucket increment/decay or that threshold was not reached; SSH trust is weakened and Windows evidence is unresolved.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Run `injectMemError` only with a mapped tuple and an owner-calculated count below the real threshold; replace `(Inaccurate)` values before execution and record counters at defined timestamps.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: CE, rank=0, below-threshold behavior, resume/wait sequence and 60/15-minute estimates are retained; counts and waits are not inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Collect machine-readable counter samples with monotonic timestamps before, during and after a bounded CE series, compute distance to threshold and observed decay over at least one approved window, and correlate logs/health without clearing evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Converts vague `several times` and `wait time windows` into auditable numerical evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A CE event does not demonstrate leaky-bucket decay or below-threshold margin.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: An incorrect threshold or count may cross escalation policy, trigger an error storm or convert the exercise into a fatal-memory test.

project_override_considerations: The labels explicitly marked `(Inaccurate)` cannot be treated as approved settings. Execution must await the platform's authoritative bucket specification.
expected_evidence: Bucket specification, counter source, threshold/window/decay rule
Target matrix, package hash and exact bounded count
Timestamped pre/injection/post/window counter series and full transcript
Windows/BMC/UEFI slot evidence plus indicators off and system health
Settings restoration, residual-error check and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Threshold and Time Window are explicitly marked inaccurate; `several times` and wait duration are unspecified; controller 1~N lacks a tuple/coverage matrix; rank is fixed at 0 without justification; Windows conflicts with dmesg; and the expected numerical decay is not defined.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Leaky-bucket decay intent is clear. The platform specification can supply numerical settings, counter semantics, targets and recovery, so static review is complete while execution remains gated.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 29 Wistron-System RAS-00749-V003: provide authoritative correctable-threshold/time-window values and units, counter source/decay rule, controller 1~N tuple/rank coverage, ITP/CScripts version/hash and CE semantics, safe below-threshold count/margin/timing, expected Windows/BMC/UEFI/indicator/health evidence, aborts, recovery and BIOS restoration.

review_improvement: Makes the numerical counter trajectory—not generic CE keywords—the decisive evidence and rejects source settings explicitly labeled inaccurate.
independent_technical_reasoning: A leaky bucket is defined by threshold, time base and decay behavior. None can be established from a single CE log, and the source itself disclaims the BIOS values as inaccurate. The injection count must be calculated with margin from the real threshold and every counter sample tied to a monotonic clock. Because an FAE can provide those parameters and the test purpose is otherwise clear, this is a gated RPUC case with a source conflict, not BLOCKED or a license to invent values.
